proposed_comments.title: Preserve redirected activations during cold startup

confidence.rationale: The current upstream code dispatches only when AppWindow is already available and otherwise logs/drops redirected activation arguments; the fork-side fix was built and cleared all review threads.

proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve redirected activations during cold startup

**Severity:** `high`

A redirected `x-cmdpal` activation can arrive after `AppInstance.Activated` is registered but before `OnLaunched` has created the `MainWindow`. In that path the current code logs and drops the activation, and because the redirecting process can exit immediately after `RedirectActivationToAsync` returns, the command link can be lost before CmdPal can process it. Please capture the activation data synchronously into a plain snapshot, queue redirected activations until startup finishes, and publish the main window only after the queued snapshots have been replayed so later redirects cannot overtake earlier ones.

proposed_comments.title: Add direct coordinator regression coverage

confidence.rationale: The coordinator is the new authorization and execution boundary, and repeated review evidence identifies its queueing, consent, cancellation, and re-resolution paths as untested.

proposed_comments.body:
### Add direct coordinator regression coverage

**Severity:** `high`

Please add focused unit tests for `ExternalCommandLinkCoordinator` before merge. The coordinator owns the security-sensitive queueing, disabled-state rechecks, remembered versus one-time consent, cancellation and timeout handling, and post-consent command re-resolution; parser and permission-store tests do not exercise those guarantees. Include cases for provider replacement and filter links so a stale or unauthorized activation cannot be dispatched or persisted.

test_instructions: Invoke an x-cmdpal command deep link while CmdPal is not already visible, including during cold startup.
Verify the command link is preserved, consent is shown when needed, and the requested command or settings route executes after CmdPal finishes launching.
Send two command links rapidly during startup and verify they are handled in arrival order rather than dropped or reordered.
